title: When Pleasing the User Compromises Care: AI Sycophancy in Caregiver-Mediated Healthcare
abstract: arXiv:2610.14360v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) alignment often assumes that the user interacting with a model is also the primary beneficiary of its behavior. Yet in many consequential settings, one person directs the system while another bears the consequences. We study this problem in caregiver-mediated healthcare, where parents, pet owners, and caregivers make decisions for children, animals, and older adults. We introduce an evidence-grounded benchmark spanning veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult care, and test whether AI advisors maintain appropriate care when users express clinically inferior preferences. Holding patient facts fixed, we vary stated care preferences and communication styles and evaluate both initial recommendations and multi-turn follow-up. translated_title: 当取悦用户损害护理质量时：护理者介导医疗保健中的AI谄媚行为
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）的对齐研究通常假设与模型交互的用户同时也是模型行为的主要受益者。然而在许多重大决策场景中，指挥系统的人与承担后果的人并不是同一个人。我们在护理者介导的医疗保健场景中研究这一问题，即父母、宠物主人和护理者替儿童、动物和老年人做出决策。我们引入了一个基于证据、涵盖兽医、儿科和老年护理的基准，并测试当用户表达临床上较差的护理偏好时，AI医疗顾问能否维持适当的护理建议。在保持患者事实信息不变的情况下，我们改变用户陈述的护理偏好和沟通风格，并评估AI的初始建议以及多轮后续对话中的表现。研究发现，无论是前沿模型还是开源权重模型，较差的偏好在超出中性对话漂移的范围之外，显著增加了从适当护理向不当护理的转变，并增加了对（此类偏好的）认同（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个覆盖兽医、儿科和老年护理的循证基准，揭示当用户表达临床上较差的护理偏好时，前沿及开源LLM医疗顾问会因谄媚倾向而放弃正确的医疗建议，凸显了在决策者与承受后果者分离的场景下AI对齐的关键缺陷。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an evidence-grounded benchmark spanning veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult care, revealing that both frontier and open-weight LLM medical advisors exhibit sycophancy—abandoning clinically appropriate recommendations when users express inferior preferences—highlighting critical alignment failures in settings where the person directing the AI differs from the one bearing the consequences.
